headline: Maui Planning Commission

meeting.summary: Maui Planning Commission recommended a Pāʻia community plan change unanimously and a zoning change for about 170 homes, 5 to 3.
meeting.recap: The vice chair led the meeting in place of Chair Ward.[[0:00:38]] The main item was a County Council proposal to change the community plan and zoning (land-use rules) for 40.392 acres in Pāʻia.[[0:02:48]] The commission was asked only for a recommendation to the council, not a final approval.[[0:09:04]] The landowner's team described about 170 homes: 120 single-family and 50 multifamily.[[0:34:34]] At least 34 would be workforce rentals kept affordable forever.[[0:35:35]] A small business owner who works in Pāʻia testified in strong support.[[1:33:39]] A Pāʻia homeowner of 25 years testified in opposition.[[1:36:35]] Commissioners voted unanimously to recommend approving the community plan change.[[5:17:06]] The planning department, which first recommended deferral, said it could now recommend zoning approval.[[5:26:00]] A motion to recommend denying the zoning change failed, 2 to 5.[[5:50:48]] Commissioners added that Maui residents should park free in the planned public lot.[[6:08:26]] Commissioners added a request that the owner commit to more community engagement in Pāʻia.[[6:16:39]] A comment asking the council to seek more affordable housing failed, 2 to 4.[[6:37:26]] The commission voted 5 to 3 to recommend approving the zoning change with conditions.[[6:52:52]]
decided: Commissioners voted unanimously to recommend that the County Council approve the community plan amendment.
A motion to recommend that the council deny the change in zoning failed.
free parking for Maui residents at the proposed public parking lot: Commissioners added to the main motion that Maui residents can park free in the planned public parking lot.
owner to commit to meaningful additional community engagement in Pāʻia: Commissioners added a request that the property owner commit to meaningful, additional community engagement in Pāʻia.
A proposed comment asking the council to request more affordable housing was not added.
The commission voted to recommend that the council approve the change in zoning with conditions, as amended.
meeting.next: The commission's attorney advised the council to hold the zoning until the state Land Use Commission approves a change from agriculture to urban. The project may return to the commission later for an SMA (coastal area) permit.

moments.q: 'We stand at the beginning of the project, not in the middle or anywhere close to the end.'
Landowner: 'I view it as a responsibility.'
A council member testifies in her personal capacity
A commissioner lays out reasons to recommend denial
Vice chair: 'the incredible lack of community engagement from the beginning'
Final vote on the zoning recommendation
